name: Emirates Islamic
founded: 1975 (incorporated 3 Oct 1975 by decree of the Ruler of Dubai as a conventional bank; re-registered as a Public Joint Stock Company in July 1995; converted to full Shariah compliance on 9 Oct 2004)
ownership_summary: Wholly owned subsidiary of Emirates NBD Bank (P.J.S.C.). ENBD held ~99.9% until 2025, then acquired the remaining minority; EI shares were suspended on DFM from 10 Jun 2025 and the bank was delisted, becoming 100% owned. Ultimate parent is Investment Corporation of Dubai, wholly owned by the Government of Dubai (EI H1 2026 financial statements, note 1).
government_link: Yes - indirectly: 100% owned by Emirates NBD, whose ultimate parent is Investment Corporation of Dubai, wholly owned by the Government of Dubai (as of 30 Jun 2026).
group_structure: Separately licensed CBUAE-regulated Islamic bank with its own board, management, Shariah function and audited/reviewed accounts, 100% owned by Emirates NBD (ae-enbd). DOUBLE COUNTING: EI's assets, deposits, financing and profit are fully consolidated into Emirates NBD Group figures - never add ae-ei to ae-enbd totals. ENBD's segment reporting allocates EI across Corporate & Institutional Banking, Retail Banking & Wealth Management and Global Markets & Treasury (ENBD H1 2026 statements, note 19 - S21). ENBD reports EI plus the ENBD Islamic window together exceed AED 250bn of Islamic assets (H1 2026, S18). EI subsidiaries: Emirates Islamic Financial Brokerage Co. LLC (100%, in process of dissolution), EI Funding Limited (Cayman SPV); consolidated SPVs EIB Sukuk Company Limited and EI CD Limited (Cayman, incorporated 21 Jul 2025).

footprint: UAE only: head office in Dubai plus 36 branches (31 Dec 2025 and 30 Jun 2026). ENBD describes EI as the third-largest Islamic bank in the UAE by assets and branch network (Strategic Report 2025).
customer_segments: Personal banking (mass, Emirati, Alpha Youth for under-18s), Advantage Banking, Priority Banking (World and Emirati packages; Priority+), Private Banking (HNWIs, families, family offices and selected institutions), business banking/SME, corporate and institutional (mid-market, government housing programmes, financial institutions). ~860K+ active customers (FY2025).
business_lines: Retail Banking & Wealth Management (personal, Priority and Private Banking, business banking; cards incl. the first Amazon co-branded card in MENA, home/auto/personal finance, wealth management services); Corporate & Institutional Banking (term, working-capital, trade, project, syndicated and structured financing, cash management, escrow, ~60 APIs); Treasury & Markets (FX incl. Wa'ad and options, profit-rate swaps, yield-enhancing deposits, equity and funds execution, sukuk, Quick Remit). AR 2025 business-model graphic shows RBWM 65%, C&IB 20%, Treasury & Markets 3%, Other 12% (basis not labelled).

capabilities.wealth_summary: EI's Retail Banking & Wealth Management unit (Head: Mohamed Al Hadi) serves Advantage, Priority (AED 500k relationship balance or AED 50k salary), Priority+ (AED 4m+) and Private Banking (average balance above AED 7.5m) clients with an entirely Shariah-compliant shelf. Private Banking offers investment advisory, execution, discretionary portfolio management and credit against sukuk and funds; EI says Private Banking AUM rose nearly 94% over two years (no amount disclosed) and the unit won Euromoney's 2026 'Middle East's Best for Client Service'. The EI+ app (86% adoption) has a Wealth tab offering Shariah-compliant global equities (from USD 100), 165+ UAE equities, 60+ fractional sukuk (minimum cut to USD 5,000 in 2025), Shariah-compliant mutual funds (from AED/USD 1,000), IPO subscriptions and, since 27 Apr 2026, digital gold and silver - EI says it is the first Islamic bank in the UAE to offer this. Priority wealth solutions also list sukuk (direct from USD 200,000), structured products, Islamic investment funds and gold certificates; fractional real estate via PRYPCO is listed as under development. EI does not publish AUM, and no robo-advisor or model portfolios were found.

private_banking.detail: EI Private Banking: investment advisory services, investment execution (Shariah-compliant asset classes), credit solutions against sukuk and funds, discretionary portfolio management (manager not named), CIO Corner insights, PB debit card. Threshold: average balance above AED 7.5m. Private Banking AUM up nearly 94% and financing portfolio roughly doubled over about two years (no absolute figures); Euromoney Private Banking Awards 2026 'Middle East's Best for Client Service'; MENA Banking Excellence Awards (Wealth & Private Banking 2025) 'Islamic Wealth Manager of the Year'.

asset_management.detail: No EI asset-management subsidiary found (EI subsidiaries are a brokerage company being dissolved and SPVs). Group asset manager Emirates NBD Asset Management (DFSA) runs Shariah-compliant funds such as Emirates Global Sukuk Fund, Emirates Islamic Money Market Fund and Emirates Islamic Global Balanced Fund, with a Shari'a board whose members include an EI Shariah board member; distribution of these funds through EI not confirmed.

brokerage.detail: Equity trading is offered in EI+ (UAE equities on DFM/ADX/Nasdaq Dubai and Shariah-compliant global equities), and the digital wealth page refers to 'EI Securities' for IPO subscriptions. EI's own brokerage subsidiary, Emirates Islamic Financial Brokerage Co. LLC, is being dissolved (FY2025 and H1 2026 statements); the executing broker for EI+ trades is not named.

digital_investing.detail: EI+ mobile app 'Wealth' tab: Shariah-compliant global equities (USD 100 min), 165+ UAE equities (DFM, ADX, Nasdaq Dubai; some restricted to UAE nationals), 60+ fractional sukuk (USD 5,000 min), Shariah-compliant mutual funds (equity, income, multi-asset, ETF funds; AED/USD 1,000 min), IPO subscriptions, digital gold and silver bars (launched 27 Apr 2026; LBMA/DGD gold incl. Emirates NBD, PAMP and Valcambi bars, UAEGD silver, vault storage, cash or physical redemption). Digital wealth was expanded to equities and sukuk in 2025; a wealth dashboard for EI non-wealth clients was delivered in 2025 (ENBD Strategic Report). No launch date found for EI+ investing overall.

advisory.detail: Private Banking offers Investment Advisory Services (diversified portfolios across regions, sectors and asset classes); Priority 'Wealth' benefit covers IPOs, equities, funds, sukuk, fractional sukuk and metals. Advisory model for Priority not described in detail on pages opened.

discretionary.detail: Discretionary Portfolio Management is listed as a Private Banking service; no description, manager or minimum published.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No robo-advisor or model/managed portfolio product found in EI+ or on EI wealth pages; app investing is self-directed.

funds_platform.detail: Shariah-compliant mutual funds in EI+ (equity, regular-income, multi-asset, ETF funds; minimum AED/USD 1,000); 'Islamic Investment Funds' in the Priority wealth menu. Fund houses and platform provider not named.

structured_products.detail: 'Structured Products' listed in the Priority Banking wealth-solutions menu; yield-enhancing deposit products (floored floater, collared floater, range accrual) offered by Treasury & Markets. No product detail or minimum published.

private_markets.detail: No private-markets/alternatives product found. Fractional real-estate investment via PRYPCO is listed as a Priority benefit but 'currently under development' and 'subject to launch'.

islamic_wealth.detail: Entire offering is Shariah-compliant (Head of Shariah: Dr. Abdulsalam Kilani): direct sukuk (sovereign, quasi-sovereign, corporate, green; from USD 200,000), fractional sukuk (60+ in app, USD 5,000 min), Shariah-screened equities and funds, digital gold/silver, gold certificates; UAE's first Shariah-compliant certificate of deposit programme (H1 2026 release).

partners.what: Fractional real-estate investment for Priority clients - listed as under development, subject to launch
FX Wa'ad dealing on Bloomberg - EI says it was the first Islamic bank live on the platform (treasury, not wealth)

initiatives.what: EI+ digital wealth proposition expanded to equities and sukuk; Fractional Sukuk minimum reduced from USD 25,000 to USD 5,000; Alpha Youth proposition; first Amazon co-branded credit card in MENA; wealth dashboard for EI non-wealth clients.
Trading in EI shares suspended on DFM after ENBD's mandatory acquisition of the remaining minority; EI delisted and became 100% ENBD-owned.
EI CD Limited incorporated; Chairman cites launch of UAE's first Shariah-compliant Certificate of Deposit Programme.
EI Private Banking named 'Middle East's Best for Client Service' (Euromoney Private Banking Awards 2026); bank states plans to expand Private Banking with focus on regional expansion and innovation.
Launched Shariah-compliant digital gold and silver investment in EI+ (first Islamic bank in UAE per EI).
H1 2026 results: total income AED 3.2bn (+8%), net profit AED 1.7bn, total assets AED 153.8bn, CET1 14.8%.

opportunities: Shariah-only shelf with no robo-advisor or model/managed portfolios found in EI+; app investing is self-directed (S8).
Private Banking AUM up nearly 94% in two years, with a stated plan to expand Private Banking regionally and through innovation (S12).
Active product build-out in the EI+ Wealth tab: equities and sukuk (2025), digital gold/silver (Apr 2026), fractional real estate pending (S5, S11, S6).
High digital adoption: EI+ used by 86% of the customer base (S5).
barriers: Islamic-only: every product needs Shariah-compliant structuring and sign-off by the Shariah function (S1, S9).

100% owned by Emirates NBD; Group has its own asset manager, brokerage and digital wealth platform (see ae-enbd), so vendor decisions may be taken or shared at Group level (inference not documented - verify).
No disclosed AUM or investing-user numbers to size the opportunity (S2, S3, S5).
incumbent_vendors: No wealth technology vendor publicly named for EI+ digital wealth (checked S8, S11, S5).
PRYPCO - fractional real estate, under development (S6).
Bloomberg - FX Wa'ad dealing platform, treasury (S5).
